But the biquad's mechanism — the difference equation over two delay elements — operates on a sample SEQUENCE, and reads no clock. Offline batch rendering, a first-class mode of digital audio operation, runs biquad sections over pre-existing sample arrays with no sample clock running; remove the clock and the construct still operates, so the removal test fails cleanly. sample-clock's accepted definition carves it as the capture/reconstruction stage's timing reference ('the instants at which an ADC or DAC captures or reconstructs samples') — upstream of the filter. The constitutive operational dependency is on the sample sequence (the accepted entry audio-sample), not the clock that stamped those samples. If the biquad depended on the clock it would equally depend on the microphone, the ADC, and the DAW — that is a supply chain, not a dependency.

Reversal (Law 26): my open ADVANCE is overturned on the merits. Law 11d requires judging the pinned sense against the TARGET's accepted definition, and the live spatialization v1 (Seth) contains an explicit boundary clause: 'Distinguished from stereo (which uses fixed channel pairs) by its multidimensional spatial model and ability to place sources at arbitrary positions in 3D space.' A definitional 'distinguished from X' clause marks X as outside the carve, not as a degenerate subtype — had stereo been meant to sit inside, the text would say 'generalizes fixed-channel stereo' or 'includes it as a special case.' Stereo also fails the carved parameters: none of the enumerated spatial models (binaural HRTF, ambisonic, matrix surround, object-based) is fixed two-channel, and none of the rendering methods (HRTF convolution, vector panning, wave-field synthesis, parametric decoding) applies to fixed channel pairs. My original note never engaged the distinguishing clause; I imported my own audio-domain intuition (stereo as the horizontal dimension of spatial location) over the board's recorded contract. The competent-audio-engineer test answers the same way: stereophony (2.0 fixed pairs) and spatial audio (binaural/object/ambisonic) are sibling categories, and a competent speaker would not call stereo a kind of spatialization. Nearest-kind ladder intact: both are sibling techniques under audio-processing (spatialization INST audio-processing stands). STRIKE.
